about: Generated by node tools/game-catalogue.mjs --write from curriculum/question-types.json and curriculum/aa-sl.json. Do not edit.

levels.0: Prior learning: algebra the IB assumes (factorising, rearranging, surds, fractions). Floor 1 warm-ups, and served when a dependent step is missed.
levels.1: Recall, 1 to 2 marks, one step. Floor 1.
levels.2: Procedure, 3 to 4 marks, one skill in a few steps. Floors 1 to 2.
levels.3: Paper 1 exam level, 5 to 6 marks, no calculator. Floors 2 to 3.
levels.4: Paper 2 exam level, 5 to 6 marks with a calculator, or a harder multi-condition Paper 1 item. Floor 3 and deeper.
levels.5: Synoptic: Section B chains, concept links and modelling. Bosses, floor 4 and deeper.

quadratic.name: One parabola in all its forms
quadratic.summary: Pick a and the two roots (or the vertex), then derive every linked quantity, so any of them can be hidden and any shown.

quantities.name: a
quantities.is: leading coefficient: the stretch, and up (a > 0) or down (a < 0)
quantities.pick: non-zero; ±1, ±2, ±1/2 on Paper 1, ±3 allowed when nothing is halved

quantities.name: p, q
quantities.is: the roots, so the x-intercepts are (p, 0) and (q, 0)
quantities.pick: integers with p < q; p + q even whenever the axis or vertex is asked

quantities.name: h
quantities.is: axis of symmetry x = h, and the x-coordinate of the vertex

quantities.name: k
quantities.is: y-coordinate of the vertex: the minimum (a > 0) or maximum (a < 0) value
quantities.pick: f(h) = −a(q − p)²/4

quantities.name: b, c
quantities.is: coefficients of the general form ax² + bx + c
quantities.pick: b = −a(p + q), c = apq

quantities.name: y-intercept
quantities.is: the point (0, c)
quantities.pick: c = apq = ah² + k

quantities.name: Δ
quantities.is: discriminant b² − 4ac
quantities.pick: a²(q − p)²

quantities.name: forms
quantities.is: general ax² + bx + c, factorised a(x − p)(x − q), vertex a(x − h)² + k
quantities.pick: all three written from a, p, q

quantities.name: range
quantities.is: y ≥ k when a > 0, y ≤ k when a < 0
quantities.pick: from a and k

quantities.name: extra point
quantities.is: (x₁, f(x₁)) used to pin down a
quantities.pick: small integer x₁, not a root and not h

quantities.name: table
quantities.is: f(x) at 5 to 7 consecutive integers
quantities.pick: centred near h so a symmetric pair of equal outputs is visible

modes: rational roots (default): all three forms exist with integer p and q
surd roots: pick integers h, k with −k/a positive and not a square, so the roots are h ± √(−k/a) and there is no rational factorised form
no real roots: pick h, k with k/a > 0, so Δ < 0 and there is no factorised form over the reals
clean: Paper 1: every value exact; with q − p even, k is an integer or a half
the extra point has small integer coordinates
on a graph, roots, vertex and y-intercept sit on grid points
roots, vertex and y-intercept are distinct points unless a view needs them to coincide

quadratic-equation.name: A quadratic equation, in context or in disguise
quadratic-equation.summary: The quadratic situation set equal to zero, wrapped in a context or a substitution that makes exactly one root unusable.

quantities.name: wrapper
quantities.is: what the quadratic stands for
quantities.pick: plain; context (lengths, a sector, probabilities that sum to 1); u = bˣ; x + c/x; a sum of logs

quantities.name: u-roots
quantities.is: the roots of the quadratic in u
quantities.pick: integers, one of them ≤ 0 when u = bˣ so it must be rejected

quantities.name: x-roots
quantities.is: the solutions of the original equation
quantities.pick: from the u-roots: x = log_b u; for logs, keep only roots with every argument positive

quantities.name: invalid root
quantities.is: the root the wrapper rules out
quantities.pick: exactly one: a negative length, a probability outside [0, 1], bˣ ≤ 0 or a log of a non-positive number

clean: Paper 1: u-roots are integers and the valid x is an integer or log_b of an integer
Paper 2 context versions may need the formula and 3 s.f.

quadratic-parameter.name: A quadratic with a parameter in it
quadratic-parameter.summary: A quadratic whose coefficients contain an unknown constant k (directly, or after equating a line and a curve), so its discriminant is an expression in k.

quantities.name: source
quantities.is: where the quadratic comes from
quantities.pick: given directly (x² + kx + 9); a line y = mx + n meeting a curve y = x² + px + r; a log or exponential equation that reduces to a quadratic

quantities.name: k
quantities.is: the parameter
quantities.pick: in b, in c, or in both

quantities.name: Δ(k)
quantities.is: the discriminant as an expression in k
quantities.pick: linear or quadratic in k; for a line meeting y = x² + px + r it is (p − m)² − 4(r − n)

quantities.name: critical k
quantities.is: the values where Δ(k) = 0
quantities.pick: integers: for the line case pick r − n = s², so m = p ± 2s

quantities.name: condition
quantities.is: what the question wants
quantities.pick: equal roots or tangent (Δ = 0), two points (Δ > 0), none (Δ < 0), real roots (Δ ≥ 0), always positive (a > 0 and Δ < 0)

quantities.name: extra condition
quantities.is: a second requirement on the roots or k
quantities.pick: same-sign roots (c/a > 0), k positive, or the log argument staying positive

quantities.name: contact point
quantities.is: where a tangent line touches
quantities.pick: x = −b/(2a) at the critical k

clean: critical k values are integers
the inequality in k factorises
say whether the boundary is included

curve-and-line.name: A curve and a line that meet
curve-and-line.summary: Pick the two meeting x-values first, then build the curve as the line plus a multiple of (x − x₁)(x − x₂), so the equated quadratic is known in advance.

quantities.name: line
quantities.is: y = mx + n, or the normal to the curve at a given point
quantities.pick: small integer m and n; m ≠ 0

quantities.name: x₁, x₂
quantities.is: the x-coordinates where they meet
quantities.pick: integers, or h ± √d with small d

quantities.name: curve
quantities.is: a quadratic y = mx + n + a(x − x₁)(x − x₂), or a rational y = c + e/(x − r) chosen to meet the line at x₁ and x₂
quantities.pick: a non-zero integer; for the rational curve r is not x₁ or x₂

quantities.name: equated quadratic
quantities.is: what equating and rearranging gives
quantities.pick: a(x − x₁)(x − x₂) = 0, expanded

quantities.name: points
quantities.is: (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) on the line
quantities.pick: y = mx + n at each

quantities.name: distance
quantities.is: length of the chord between the points
quantities.pick: |x₂ − x₁|·√(1 + m²)

clean: Paper 1: integer or simple surd x-values; choose m = 0, ±1, ±2 or ±3 so √(1 + m²) is small
the final surd simplifies to a√b

quadratic-inequality.name: A quadratic compared with a number
quadratic-inequality.summary: The quadratic situation with an inequality sign and, sometimes, a right-hand side to move across first.

quantities.name: sign
quantities.is: which inequality

quantities.name: right-hand side
quantities.is: the value f(x) is compared with
quantities.pick: 0, or a constant d with f(x) − d still factorising

quantities.name: solution set
quantities.is: one interval between the roots, two rays outside them, all x, or no x
quantities.pick: from the sign of a, the roots and the sign

quantities.name: context bound
quantities.is: the largest or smallest whole number allowed
quantities.pick: Paper 2: non-integer roots, so the rounding direction matters

clean: Paper 1 roots are integers or simple fractions
Paper 2 roots are not integers, so the integer answer is a real decision

quadratic-model.name: A quadratic model in context
quadratic-model.summary: A projectile height h(t) or an area A(x) under a fixed-length constraint, built from the vertex so the optimum is clean.

quantities.name: context
quantities.is: what is modelled
quantities.pick: height of a thrown object over time; area of a pen with a fixed length of fence (with or without a wall)

quantities.name: peak
quantities.is: time and height of the maximum, or the width and area of the best pen
quantities.pick: vertex (T, H) with integer or half-integer T

quantities.name: a
quantities.is: how fast the curve bends
quantities.pick: height: −5 or −4.9 (Paper 2); area: −1 or −2 from the constraint

quantities.name: start value
quantities.is: height at t = 0
quantities.pick: h(0) = aT² + H

quantities.name: landing time
quantities.is: positive root of h(t) = 0
quantities.pick: T + √(−H/a); the negative root is rejected

quantities.name: constraint
quantities.is: fixed perimeter L
quantities.pick: pen against a wall: A(x) = x(L − 2x), best x = L/4; free pen: A(x) = x(L/2 − x), best x = L/4 (a square)

clean: Paper 1: integer vertex and an integer or surd landing time
Paper 2: a = −4.9 and answers to 3 s.f.

exp-model.name: An exponential model in context
exp-model.summary: Pick the start value, the growth factor (or rate k) and, for limited growth, the long-run value; then derive every value, time and rate, so any of them can be hidden.

quantities.name: form
quantities.is: how the model is written
quantities.pick: P₀·aᵗ (a growth factor such as 1.04 or 0.85); A·e^(kt); C + A·e^(−kt) (cooling, limited growth); P₀·a^(t − t₀) when time is counted from a start year

quantities.name: P₀
quantities.is: the value at t = 0
quantities.pick: P₀ for the first two forms, C + A for the limited form; a round number such as 200, 500, 2000

quantities.name: a or k
quantities.is: the growth factor per unit time, or the continuous rate
quantities.pick: a = 1 + r from a whole-number percentage r; k = ln(a), or k = ±ln 2/T from a half-life or doubling time T

quantities.name: r
quantities.is: the percentage change per unit time
quantities.pick: a − 1 written as a percentage: 1.04 is +4%, 0.85 is −15%

quantities.name: T
quantities.is: the half-life or doubling time
quantities.pick: a whole number of units; k = ln 2/T exactly

quantities.name: C
quantities.is: the long-run value: the horizontal asymptote of the limited model
quantities.pick: room temperature, a carrying level; 0 for the plain forms

quantities.name: data point
quantities.is: a second value (t₁, P(t₁)) used to find k or a
quantities.pick: chosen so P(t₁)/P₀ (or (P(t₁) − C)/A) is a simple ratio such as 1/2, 2, 3/4

quantities.name: prediction
quantities.is: P at a later time t₂
quantities.pick: computed from the model; 3 s.f. on Paper 2

quantities.name: threshold
quantities.is: a level L the model reaches
quantities.pick: strictly between the start value and the long-run value, so the time is positive

quantities.name: threshold time
quantities.is: when P = L
quantities.pick: t = ln((L − C)/A)/k; the first whole unit after it when whole units are asked

quantities.name: table
quantities.is: P at equally spaced times
quantities.pick: shows a constant ratio between neighbours (constant ratio of P − C for the limited form)

modes: growth factor form P₀·aᵗ (percent per unit time)
continuous form A·e^(kt) with k from a half-life or a data point
limited form C + A·e^(−kt), with the long-run value C
base-10 log model (a scale such as loudness or acidity): L = m·log₁₀(x/x₀), solved by turning it back into a power
clean: Paper 1: k is an exact log (ln 2/5, ln 3/4) and times are exact logs
Paper 2: answers to 3 s.f., with whole-unit answers rounded in the direction the context needs
the threshold is between the start and the long-run value, so the time is positive

exp-growth-vs-linear.name: Linear and exponential growth side by side
exp-growth-vs-linear.summary: The growth-factor model next to a linear model with the same start value, shown in tables, graphs and words, so the two growth patterns can be compared.

quantities.name: linear partner
quantities.is: y = P₀ + d·t, adding the same amount d each step
quantities.pick: d a whole number; often d = P₀·r so both agree after one step

quantities.name: constant difference
quantities.is: the step added each time by the linear model
quantities.pick: d

quantities.name: constant ratio
quantities.is: the factor applied each time by the exponential model
quantities.pick: a

quantities.name: overtaking time
quantities.is: when the exponential passes the linear model for good
quantities.pick: the first whole step where P₀·aⁿ > P₀ + d·n

quantities.name: table
quantities.is: both models at t = 0, 1, 2, …
quantities.pick: 5 to 7 steps, wide enough to show the overtaking

clean: table values are whole numbers or have at most 2 decimal places
the overtaking step is inside the table

exp-log-pair.name: An exponential function and its log inverse
exp-log-pair.summary: Pick a base and a translation, then write f(x) = b^(x − h) + c and its inverse log_b(x − c) + h (or the other way round), with input values that give whole-number powers.

quantities.name: b
quantities.is: the base
quantities.pick: 2, 3, 4, 8, 10 or e; bases from one family (2, 4, 8) when change of base is the point

quantities.name: h, c
quantities.is: the translation (h, c) of the parent b^x, or of log_b x
quantities.pick: small integers

quantities.name: A
quantities.is: a vertical stretch or reflection in front
quantities.pick: 1 by default; 2, 3, −1 or 1/2 for graph questions

quantities.name: exp form
quantities.is: f(x) = A·b^(x − h) + c
quantities.pick: y-intercept A·b^(−h) + c, asymptote y = c, range y > c when A > 0

quantities.name: log form
quantities.is: g(x) = log_b(x − h) + c
quantities.pick: vertical asymptote x = h, domain x > h, x-intercept h + b^(−c), range all real numbers

quantities.name: inverse
quantities.is: the other form, found by swapping x and y
quantities.pick: f⁻¹(x) = log_b((x − c)/A) + h for the exp form; g⁻¹(x) = b^(x − c) + h for the log form

quantities.name: evaluation points
quantities.is: inputs where the answer is exact
quantities.pick: x − h a whole power of b for logs; any small integer for exponentials

quantities.name: partner function
quantities.is: a second exp or log function to compose with
quantities.pick: log_b x, ln x, or an exponential in a base from the same family

quantities.name: composite
quantities.is: f(g(x)) or g(f(x)), simplified with log laws
quantities.pick: such as 4^(log₂ x) = x²

modes: exponential given, log is the inverse
log given, exponential is the inverse
two bases from one family, for change of base
clean: evaluation points give whole-number powers
asymptotes and intercepts sit on grid points on a graph

log-function.name: A transformed log function
log-function.summary: The log form with a linear inside, y = A·log_b(mx + n) + c, so the asymptote and domain come from mx + n = 0.

quantities.name: m, n
quantities.is: the linear expression inside the log
quantities.pick: m from ±1, ±2, ±3; n chosen so −n/m is an integer or a simple fraction

quantities.name: x₀
quantities.is: the zero of the inside: the vertical asymptote x = x₀
quantities.pick: −n/m

quantities.name: domain
quantities.is: where mx + n > 0
quantities.pick: x > x₀ when m > 0, x < x₀ when m < 0

quantities.name: x-intercept
quantities.is: where A·log_b(mx + n) + c = 0
quantities.pick: mx + n = b^(−c/A), chosen to be exact

quantities.name: sign region
quantities.is: where log_b(mx + n) is positive
quantities.pick: mx + n > 1; it is negative where 0 < mx + n < 1

quantities.name: extra factor
quantities.is: a positive factor next to the log, such as a power of x in a fraction
quantities.pick: positive on the domain, so the sign of the whole expression is the sign of the log

clean: x₀ is an integer or a half
the x-intercept is exact

log-quadratic.name: The log of a downward quadratic
log-quadratic.summary: The quadratic situation with a < 0, put inside a log: f(x) = log_k(g(x)). The roots give the domain and asymptotes, g(x) = 1 gives the zeros, and the vertex gives the maximum.

quantities.name: g(x)
quantities.is: the quadratic inside the log
quantities.pick: a(x − p)(x − q) with a < 0 and integer roots p < q

quantities.name: domain
quantities.is: where g(x) > 0
quantities.pick: p < x < q

quantities.name: asymptotes
quantities.is: the vertical asymptotes
quantities.pick: x = p and x = q

quantities.name: G
quantities.is: the vertex height of g: the largest value inside the log
quantities.pick: G = −a(q − p)²/4, chosen as a whole power of the base

quantities.name: k
quantities.is: the base of the log
quantities.pick: such that G = kⁿ for a small whole n

quantities.name: maximum
quantities.is: the largest value of f
quantities.pick: log_k G = n at x = h, the axis of the parabola

quantities.name: zeros
quantities.is: where g(x) = 1
quantities.pick: h ± √(h² − (apq − 1)/a) in general; chosen so the surd is small, such as 3 ± √3

quantities.name: sign
quantities.is: where f is positive or negative
quantities.pick: positive between the zeros, negative between each zero and its asymptote

clean: roots p and q are integers with q − p even
G = kⁿ with n = 1, 2 or 3
G/n differs from the true base, so a divided answer is wrong
the zeros are h ± √d with d small and not a square

gdc-curve.name: One awkward curve on a closed domain
gdc-curve.summary: Pick a function that mixes families and a domain, then let the GDC fix every feature: zeros, turning points, y-intercept and endpoints, none at simple values.

quantities.name: family
quantities.is: the kind of function
quantities.pick: exponential plus linear (a·e^(bx) + mx + c); a cubic or quartic with decimal coefficients; a bell curve a·e^(−bx²) + c; a product such as (x + 2)(x − 3)e^(−x/2); a composite with sine or cosine; a log or rational term

quantities.name: domain
quantities.is: d₁ ≤ x ≤ d₂
quantities.pick: integers or simple decimals, wide enough to hold every feature asked for

quantities.name: zeros
quantities.is: the x-intercepts inside the domain
quantities.pick: found numerically; one to three, each a clean crossing, given to 3 s.f.

quantities.name: y-intercept
quantities.is: (0, f(0)) when 0 is in the domain
quantities.pick: evaluated exactly, then to 3 s.f.

quantities.name: turning points
quantities.is: local maximum and minimum points inside the domain
quantities.pick: found numerically; one or two, coordinates to 3 s.f.

quantities.name: endpoints
quantities.is: (d₁, f(d₁)) and (d₂, f(d₂))
quantities.pick: evaluated, to 3 s.f.

quantities.name: greatest and least values
quantities.is: the extremes of f on the domain
quantities.pick: the largest and smallest of the turning values and the endpoint values

quantities.name: asymptote
quantities.is: a vertical asymptote x = r, in the log or rational mode only
quantities.pick: r outside the domain or at one end of it

quantities.name: window
quantities.is: a GDC window that shows every feature
quantities.pick: x from d₁ to d₂; y from a little below the least value to a little above the greatest

quantities.name: table
quantities.is: f at a fixed step across the domain
quantities.pick: step 0.5 or 1, so each zero shows as a sign change

quantities.name: wrong graphs
quantities.is: three wrong options for pick-the-graph
quantities.pick: each changes one thing: drawn past the domain, a turning point moved by a squashed window, a crossed asymptote, or a zero read as the y-intercept

modes: mixed family (default): no zero or turning point at a simple value, so the GDC is the intended route
factorised product: zeros read from the factors, turning points need the GDC
x-factor: f(x) = x·g(x), so x = 0 is one zero and dividing by x loses it
endpoint extreme: the greatest or least value on the domain is at an endpoint, not at the turning point
asymptote: a log or rational term puts a vertical asymptote at or just outside one end of the domain
clean: Paper 2: every value to 3 s.f., and no feature rounds to a whole number by accident
features at least 0.5 apart in x and clearly apart in y, so the four options can be told apart
the whole graph fits a window with a y-range of about 20 units or less
every zero is a crossing, not a touch

gdc-two-curves.name: Two curves that meet
gdc-two-curves.summary: Two functions from different families (or two models, or f and its inverse) that cross one to three times in the window, so the crossings need the GDC.

quantities.name: f, g
quantities.is: the two functions
quantities.pick: two models of time (tanks, populations, tides); an exponential and a quadratic; a curve and a line; f and f⁻¹

quantities.name: context
quantities.is: what x and y mean, with units, and the interval of interest
quantities.pick: time t ≥ 0 in hours or days, or a plain domain

quantities.name: crossings
quantities.is: the meeting points (xᵢ, yᵢ)
quantities.pick: found numerically; one to three in the window, each y computed from the unrounded x

quantities.name: difference
quantities.is: h(x) = f(x) − g(x)
quantities.pick: its zeros are exactly the xᵢ

quantities.name: chord
quantities.is: the distance between two crossing points
quantities.pick: √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²), from stored values

quantities.name: parameter
quantities.is: a constant in g fixed by one known crossing
quantities.pick: optional: pick a nice x₀ and set the constant so g(x₀) = f(x₀); the other crossings still need the GDC

quantities.name: table
quantities.is: f and g side by side at a fixed step
quantities.pick: the sign of f − g changes between rows at each crossing

modes: two models in context (default)
curve and line
function and inverse: when f is increasing every crossing lies on y = x, so intersecting f with y = x is enough
one crossing hidden outside the standard window (a large x or a large y)
clean: crossings at least 0.3 apart in x and at a clear angle, never a near-tangent
no crossing within 0.05 of a window edge unless that is the point of the view
Paper 2: 3 s.f.; y from the unrounded x

gdc-combined.name: A new function built from two given ones
gdc-combined.summary: The two-curves situation plus a function made from them: their difference or sum, or the distance from a fixed point to a curve, whose extreme or zero the GDC finds.

quantities.name: combined
quantities.is: the new function
quantities.pick: D(x) = f(x) − g(x) (or g − f), S(x) = f(x) + g(x), or d(x) = √((x − x₀)² + (f(x) − y₀)²) from a point P(x₀, y₀)

quantities.name: extreme
quantities.is: the greatest or least value of the combined function, and where
quantities.pick: inside the domain, found with the GDC; not at a turning point of f or of g

quantities.name: zeros
quantities.is: where D = 0
quantities.pick: the crossings of f and g

quantities.name: closest point
quantities.is: the point on the curve nearest to P, in distance mode
quantities.pick: (x*, f(x*)) where d is least

quantities.name: meaning
quantities.is: what the extreme or zero says in context
quantities.pick: the largest lead, the time the totals match, the shortest path

quantities.name: whole-number answer
quantities.is: the first whole day, year or item that satisfies a condition
quantities.pick: optional; the exact crossing is not a whole number

modes: difference of two models (default)
distance from a point (often the origin) to a curve
sum of two models: a combined total
clean: the extreme is strictly inside the domain, unless the endpoint is the point of the view
the extreme of D is clearly away from the extremes of f and g, so the "own maximum" mistake gives a different number
Paper 2: 3 s.f.

gdc-context-equation.name: An equation from a context that only the GDC can solve
gdc-context-equation.summary: A model or a diagram leads to an equation that mixes families (an angle and its sine, an exponential and a polynomial), with exactly one root that makes sense in the context.

quantities.name: source
quantities.is: where the equation comes from
quantities.pick: a sector or segment area; a triangle with a given area; a velocity that is zero or equals a value; two non-linear equations in two unknowns; a savings or growth model

quantities.name: equation
quantities.is: the equation to solve
quantities.pick: mixes families, e.g. x − 3 sin x = 0, or 12.5(θ − sin θ) = 10

quantities.name: interval
quantities.is: the values the context allows
quantities.pick: 0 < θ < π for an angle in a triangle, t ≥ 0 for time, r > 0 for a length

quantities.name: roots
quantities.is: every root in a wide window
quantities.pick: found numerically

quantities.name: answer
quantities.is: the root the context wants
quantities.pick: the one in the interval, or the first one for "first time", to 3 s.f.

quantities.name: constant
quantities.is: a number in the equation a reversed view can ask for
quantities.pick: chosen so a given root is exact, such as the k that makes x = 1.5 a root of x = k sin x

modes: one root in the context interval (default)
two or more roots, only one valid in context
whole-number answer: the first full year or the smallest number of items
clean: no exact root, so technology is genuinely needed
a rejected root is clearly outside the interval, not on its edge
Paper 2: 3 s.f.

graph-from-features.name: A graph from features already found
graph-from-features.summary: Earlier parts find exact features (intercepts, vertex, stationary point, asymptote, endpoints) without a calculator; the view asks for the sketch that shows them.

quantities.name: family
quantities.is: the kind of graph
quantities.pick: a quadratic built as in `quadratic` (a, roots, vertex); a quadratic velocity on 0 ≤ t ≤ T; a curve that levels off (a + b·e^(−x), or x·e^(−x) with its maximum); a sine or cosine on a closed interval

quantities.name: features
quantities.is: what the sketch must show
quantities.pick: intercepts, the vertex or stationary points, an asymptote, the endpoints; all exact

quantities.name: domain
quantities.is: where the graph is drawn
quantities.pick: all real x, or a closed interval that includes every feature

quantities.name: shape facts
quantities.is: which way it opens, where it rises and falls, where it levels off
quantities.pick: from the sign of a, or from the context

quantities.name: wrong graphs
quantities.is: three wrong options for pick-the-graph
quantities.pick: each breaks one thing: opens the wrong way, a pointed vertex, the vertex put at the y-intercept, a level-off drawn as a turning point, or a quantity drawn below its limit

modes: quadratic (default): roots and vertex at integers or halves
restricted domain: a velocity or a model, with endpoint values to label
asymptote: a curve that levels off towards a horizontal line
conditions only: a few facts in words (a point, a zero, increasing or decreasing), so many graphs fit
clean: Paper 1: features at integers or simple fractions
the domain includes every feature the sketch must show
the features are distinct points

graph-match.name: One equation and four graphs
graph-match.summary: Pick an equation from a familiar family with small integer parameters, then draw it and three near-misses, each wrong in one checkable feature.

quantities.name: equation
quantities.is: the function
quantities.pick: linear, quadratic (any form), exponential growth or decay a·bˣ + c, logarithmic, or reciprocal a/(x − h) + k

quantities.name: facts
quantities.is: what can be checked without plotting
quantities.pick: the y-intercept, the zeros, which way a parabola opens, growth or decay, the asymptotes

quantities.name: options
quantities.is: four graphs
quantities.pick: the right one, and three that each break one fact: wrong y-intercept, growth for decay, opening the wrong way, an asymptote moved

clean: intercepts and asymptotes on grid lines
each wrong graph differs in exactly one fact

gdc-inequality.name: Two curves compared
gdc-inequality.summary: The two-curves situation with an inequality: where one graph is above the other, read from the crossings.

quantities.name: sign
quantities.is: which inequality

quantities.name: solution set
quantities.is: where the inequality holds
quantities.pick: intervals between crossings and domain ends; one piece or two

quantities.name: context
quantities.is: the question in words
quantities.pick: "when does the population exceed 1000", "for which times is tank A fuller"

clean: crossings not at whole numbers, so the boundaries are 3 s.f. values
in two-piece mode the two parts are clearly separate

composite-pair.name: Two rules chained together
composite-pair.summary: Pick an inner rule g and an outer rule f, then derive both composites, a value, a target and any hidden constant, so either rule or the composite can be hidden.

quantities.name: g
quantities.is: the inner rule, applied first in f∘g
quantities.pick: linear ax + b with small integers, a ≠ 0 and a ≠ 1

quantities.name: f
quantities.is: the outer rule, applied second
quantities.pick: linear, a square such as x² + c or (x − h)², a cubic, or a trig function on Paper 2

quantities.name: k
quantities.is: an unknown constant in one of the rules
quantities.pick: in f or in g; chosen so the solved value is an integer, often a ± pair from k² = n²

quantities.name: f∘g, g∘f
quantities.is: both composites, simplified
quantities.pick: f(g(x)) and g(f(x)); they differ unless the pair was picked to commute

quantities.name: x₀
quantities.is: the input for a value question
quantities.pick: a small integer

quantities.name: value
quantities.is: (f∘g)(x₀)
quantities.pick: computed inside out: g(x₀) first, then f of that

quantities.name: target
quantities.is: a number the composite is set equal to
quantities.pick: reached at integer x; two x-values when f squares

quantities.name: stated form
quantities.is: a form such as px² + qx + r that the composite must match
quantities.pick: expanded from the composite, so equating one coefficient gives a quadratic in the constant with integer roots

modes: forward (default): f and g given, the composite or its value asked
reversed inner: f and f∘g given, g asked; f is linear so g = (h(x) − b)/a is a polynomial
reversed outer: g and f∘g given, f asked; g is linear so u = g(x) can be undone
self: f∘f from a single rule
identity: g is f⁻¹, so both composites simplify to x
clean: Paper 1: integer coefficients and integer solutions
the order of composition is always stated in symbols or words

composite-graph-table.name: A function read from a graph or a table
composite-graph-table.summary: A graph of f through grid points, or a table of f and g, built so that every composite and inverse reading lands on a shown value.

quantities.name: f
quantities.is: a function shown as a graph or as table entries
quantities.pick: piecewise-linear through grid points, or 4 to 6 table entries

quantities.name: g
quantities.is: a second function in the table
quantities.pick: its outputs are inputs of f wherever a composite is asked

quantities.name: readings
quantities.is: f(a) and g(a)
quantities.pick: grid points or table entries

quantities.name: composites
quantities.is: (f∘f)(a) and (f∘g)(a)
quantities.pick: the inner output is itself a shown input

quantities.name: inverse values
quantities.is: f⁻¹(b)
quantities.pick: b is a shown output, and f is one-to-one on the shown domain

quantities.name: domain and range
quantities.is: the shown domain of f, and its range (the domain of f⁻¹)
quantities.pick: endpoints on grid points

quantities.name: final equation
quantities.is: f⁻¹(px + q) = c
quantities.pick: f(c) is on the graph, and x = (f(c) − q)/p is an integer

quantities.name: turning point
quantities.is: where the graph turns back, in the not-one-to-one mode
quantities.pick: a grid point

modes: one-to-one (default): f always increases or always decreases, so every inverse reading is unique
turns back: f rises then falls (or the reverse), so f(x) = k can have two answers and the domain must be cut before f has an inverse
clean: every queried value is a grid point or a table entry
the scale is 1 unit per square unless a view tests reading the scale

inverse-rule.name: A one-to-one function and its inverse
inverse-rule.summary: Pick f from a family with a domain that makes it one-to-one, then derive f⁻¹ and swap the domain and range, so f, f⁻¹ or a constant can be hidden.

quantities.name: family
quantities.is: the kind of rule
quantities.pick: linear ax + b; rational (ax + b)/(cx + d); root √(px + q) + r; quadratic (x − h)² + k on one side of its vertex; exponential e^(px) + q

quantities.name: domain of f
quantities.is: the stated domain
quantities.pick: all real x; x ≠ −d/c; x ≥ −q/p; x ≥ h or x ≤ h

quantities.name: range of f
quantities.is: the outputs f reaches
quantities.pick: from the asymptote y = a/c, the endpoint value r, the vertex value k, or the asymptote y = q

quantities.name: f⁻¹
quantities.is: the inverse rule
quantities.pick: linear (x − b)/a; rational (−dx + b)/(cx − a); root ((x − r)² − q)/p; quadratic h + √(x − k) or h − √(x − k) to match the domain; exponential ln(x − q)/p

quantities.name: domain and range of f⁻¹
quantities.is: swapped from f
quantities.pick: domain of f⁻¹ = range of f; range of f⁻¹ = domain of f

quantities.name: asymptotes
quantities.is: for the rational family
quantities.pick: f has x = −d/c and y = a/c; f⁻¹ has x = a/c and y = −d/c

quantities.name: self-inverse case
quantities.is: a rational f that is its own inverse
quantities.pick: d = −a, with ad − bc ≠ 0

quantities.name: reflection case
quantities.is: f⁻¹ equal to f reflected in the y-axis and then the x-axis
quantities.pick: rational with d = a, or f(x) = x + b; then f⁻¹(x) = −f(−x)

modes: linear or rational (default): every real x but one
root: the domain starts where px + q = 0, and the range starts at r
restricted quadratic: the domain is cut at the vertex
exponential: the range stops at the asymptote y = q
clean: integer coefficients
ad − bc ≠ 0 for the rational family
domain endpoints and asymptotes are integers

inverse-order-undo.name: Chaining, undoing and cutting a domain
inverse-order-undo.summary: The composite pair, plus a rule that is not one-to-one and the cut that fixes it, so the order of composition and the reason inverses need one-to-one rules can both be probed.

quantities.name: two-to-one rule
quantities.is: a rule that sends two inputs to one output
quantities.pick: (x − h)² + k on all real x

quantities.name: cut
quantities.is: the restriction that makes it one-to-one
quantities.pick: x ≥ h or x ≤ h

quantities.name: inverse branch
quantities.is: the inverse that matches the cut
quantities.pick: h + √(x − k) for x ≥ h; h − √(x − k) for x ≤ h

quantities.name: undo order
quantities.is: the inverse of a composite
quantities.pick: (f∘g)⁻¹ = g⁻¹∘f⁻¹, undone in reverse order

clean: h and k small integers
test inputs either side of h give the same output

rational-function.name: One linear-over-linear function in all its forms
rational-function.summary: Pick the asymptotes and the stretch first, then write the function as (ax + b)/(cx + d) and as a transformed 1/x, so every asymptote, intercept and branch is known before anything is hidden.

quantities.name: h
quantities.is: the vertical asymptote x = h, where the denominator is zero
quantities.pick: an integer, or a simple fraction −d/c when c ≠ 1

quantities.name: A
quantities.is: the horizontal asymptote y = A, the ratio a/c of the x-coefficients
quantities.pick: an integer, or a simple fraction when c ≠ 1

quantities.name: B
quantities.is: the stretch in A + B/(x − h): which pair of opposite corners the branches sit in, and how far out
quantities.pick: a non-zero integer; B = (bc − ad)/c²; B > 0 puts the branches top-right and bottom-left of the asymptotes

quantities.name: a, b, c, d
quantities.is: the coefficients of (ax + b)/(cx + d)
quantities.pick: c = 1, 2 or 3; then a = Ac, d = −hc and b = Bc − ah; ad − bc ≠ 0 always, since B ≠ 0

quantities.name: x-intercept
quantities.is: where the numerator is zero: (−b/a, 0)
quantities.pick: h − B/A; none when A = 0 (a = 0)

quantities.name: y-intercept
quantities.pick: A − B/h; none when h = 0, because then the vertical asymptote is the y-axis

quantities.name: domain and range
quantities.is: x ≠ h and y ≠ A
quantities.pick: from h and A

quantities.name: reciprocal
quantities.is: y = 1/f(x) = (cx + d)/(ax + b)
quantities.pick: its vertical asymptote is the x-intercept of f, its zero is h, and its horizontal asymptote is 1/A

quantities.name: second curve
quantities.is: a line y = k, a line y = mx + n, or a parabola, to count meeting points with
quantities.pick: chosen so it crosses each branch a clear number of times; one version touches a branch (a tangent)

quantities.name: inequality
quantities.is: f(x) compared with 0 or with a constant k
quantities.pick: boundaries at the x-intercept (or where f = k) and at x = h, so the answer has two pieces

quantities.name: wrong graphs
quantities.is: the three wrong options in pick-the-graph
quantities.pick: built from one slip each: B with the wrong sign, x = −h for the asymptote, the asymptotes swapped, the x-intercept put at x = h, or a branch drawn across x = h

quantities.name: table
quantities.is: f at a few x close to h on both sides and at large x
quantities.pick: shows the jump at x = h and the levelling off at y = A

modes: monic denominator (default): c = 1, so h and A are integers
scaled: c = 2 or 3, so the asymptotes may be fractions such as x = −1/2
letters: some of a, b, c, d are left as letters, found from given asymptotes or an intercept, or kept in the answer
through the origin: b = 0, so both intercepts are (0, 0)
clean: Paper 1: intercepts are integers or halves and thirds
h ≠ 0 and A ≠ 0 unless the view is about a missing intercept
on a graph, the asymptotes and intercepts sit on grid lines
the x-intercept is not on the vertical asymptote and the y-intercept is not on the horizontal one

rational-model.name: A linear-over-linear model in context
rational-model.summary: An average cost, a mixture being topped up, or a level that settles, built so the long-run value is the horizontal asymptote and the target is reached at a clean or a rounded input.

quantities.name: context
quantities.is: what is modelled
quantities.pick: average cost per item: A(n) = (F + vn)/n; concentration as liquid is added: C(x) = (s + px)/(V + x); a population or level that settles: P(t) = (Lt + P₀k)/(t + k)

quantities.name: long-run value
quantities.is: the horizontal asymptote and what it means
quantities.pick: v, p or L: the cost per item, the strength of what is added, the settling level

quantities.name: start value
quantities.is: the value at the input 0, when it exists
quantities.pick: C(0) = s/V, P(0) = P₀; the average cost has no value at n = 0

quantities.name: vertical asymptote
quantities.is: where the denominator is zero
quantities.pick: n = 0 or a negative input, outside the sensible domain

quantities.name: target
quantities.is: a value the model must pass
quantities.pick: between the start value and the long-run value, so it is reached

quantities.name: input for target
quantities.is: when the target is reached
quantities.pick: from a linear equation after clearing the fraction; a whole number of items is rounded the way the condition needs

clean: F, v, s, V, p are friendly integers or one decimal place
the input for the target is an integer or forces a real rounding decision
Paper 2 versions give answers to 3 s.f.

rational-asymptote-gallery.name: Curves with asymptotes, side by side
rational-asymptote-gallery.summary: A small set of curves with horizontal or vertical asymptotes, some of which cross their horizontal asymptote and some of which cannot, plus one model whose asymptote has a meaning.

quantities.name: linear over linear
quantities.is: f(x) = A + B/(x − h)
quantities.pick: from the rational-function situation; never meets y = A, because B/(x − h) is never 0

quantities.name: crossing curve
quantities.is: a curve that meets its horizontal asymptote
quantities.pick: x/(x² + 1) or x·e^(−x), both with asymptote y = 0 and both through (0, 0); or A + x/(x² + 1), which meets y = A at x = 0

quantities.name: exponential or log
quantities.is: e^x + q or ln(x − p)
quantities.pick: asymptote y = q or x = p, never crossed

quantities.name: gap, not asymptote
quantities.is: (ax + b)/(cx + d) with ad = bc
quantities.pick: for example (2x + 4)/(x + 2), which is 2 everywhere except x = −2

quantities.name: model
quantities.is: a quantity that settles
quantities.pick: from the rational-model situation, with its asymptote as the long-run value

clean: every example is checked by substituting numbers
crossing points are at integer x

basic-function.name: One function, its inputs and its outputs
basic-function.summary: Pick a family and small coefficients, then derive the outputs at chosen inputs, the intercepts, the domain and the range, so any of them can be hidden.

quantities.name: family
quantities.is: the kind of rule
quantities.pick: linear, quadratic, cubic, square root, rational (ax + b)/(cx + d), exponential, or a model in context

quantities.name: f
quantities.is: the rule
quantities.pick: small integer coefficients; a model gets a context such as a height h(t), a cost C(n) or a population P(t)

quantities.name: inputs
quantities.is: the values to substitute
quantities.pick: whole numbers including a negative; 0 for the start value; a decimal such as 1.5 on Paper 2

quantities.name: outputs
quantities.is: f at each input
quantities.pick: computed; whole numbers or simple fractions on Paper 1

quantities.name: y-intercept
quantities.is: the point (0, f(0))
quantities.pick: f(0), when 0 is in the domain

quantities.name: zeros
quantities.is: the inputs where f(x) = 0
quantities.pick: integers for polynomials, picked first and expanded

quantities.name: domain
quantities.is: the inputs allowed
quantities.pick: the natural domain (square root ≥ 0, log argument > 0, denominator ≠ 0), or a stated interval, or what the context allows

quantities.name: range
quantities.is: the outputs reached
quantities.pick: from the vertex, the asymptote, or the endpoint values

quantities.name: table
quantities.is: f at 5 to 7 inputs
quantities.pick: consecutive whole numbers, or the times a model is measured

quantities.name: test point
quantities.is: a point (x₁, y₁) to compare with the graph
quantities.pick: y₁ close to f(x₁) but not equal, so the substitution decides

modes: plain rule
model in context, with units and a sensible domain
graph or table only, with no rule shown
clean: Paper 1: outputs are integers or simple fractions
Paper 2: outputs to 3 s.f.
every input lies inside the domain unless the view asks about one outside it

basic-restricted.name: A function on a restricted domain, or a changed one
basic-restricted.summary: The basic function with a stated domain, a reflection or translation applied, or a second function to compose with, so the range has to be worked out rather than read off.

quantities.name: restriction
quantities.is: the stated domain a ≤ x ≤ b, or x ≥ a
quantities.pick: integer endpoints; for a quadratic, sometimes with the vertex inside

quantities.name: end values
quantities.is: f(a) and f(b)
quantities.pick: computed

quantities.name: turning value
quantities.is: the vertex height when the vertex is inside the restriction
quantities.pick: the minimum or maximum of the range

quantities.name: asymptote value
quantities.is: the value a rational or exponential function never reaches
quantities.pick: excluded from the range

quantities.name: transformation
quantities.is: a change applied to f
quantities.pick: g = −f (reflection in the x-axis), or f(x) + d

quantities.name: outer function
quantities.is: g, applied to the outputs of f
quantities.pick: a square root √(x − c), a log ln(x − c) or 1/(x − c), so g(f(x)) needs the range of f to fit the domain of g

quantities.name: inverse
quantities.is: f⁻¹ when f is one-to-one on the restriction
quantities.pick: its domain is the range of f

clean: endpoints and turning values are integers
each endpoint is deliberately included or excluded

basic-one-to-one.name: A one-to-one function and its inverse
basic-one-to-one.summary: The basic function chosen one-to-one, with key points on grid points, so the inverse graph comes from swapping coordinates.

quantities.name: f
quantities.is: a one-to-one function
quantities.pick: linear, a root, an exponential, a log, a rational, or a quadratic on half its domain

quantities.name: key points
quantities.is: intercepts, endpoints and one or two more points
quantities.pick: (p, q) on grid points

quantities.name: swapped points
quantities.is: the matching points on f⁻¹
quantities.pick: (q, p)

quantities.name: asymptotes
quantities.is: any asymptote of f
quantities.pick: y = c on f becomes x = c on f⁻¹

quantities.name: meeting points
quantities.is: where f and f⁻¹ meet
quantities.pick: on y = x for an increasing f: solve f(x) = x

quantities.name: area
quantities.is: the region between f and f⁻¹
quantities.pick: twice the region between f and y = x, when they meet on y = x

clean: key points on grid points
meeting points with integer coordinates

basic-relation.name: A relation that may or may not be a function
basic-relation.summary: Pick a rule, a set of pairs or a curve; some give one output per input and some do not, and some functions are one-to-one and some are not.

quantities.name: form
quantities.is: how the relation is shown
quantities.pick: a graph, a mapping diagram, a table of pairs, or an equation such as x² + y² = 9 or y² = x

quantities.name: function?
quantities.is: whether each input has exactly one output
quantities.pick: yes or no; about half of each

quantities.name: one-to-one?
quantities.is: whether each output comes from only one input
quantities.pick: for the functions only

quantities.name: witness
quantities.is: the input with two outputs, or the output with two inputs
quantities.pick: a specific value, used in the reason

quantities.name: restriction
quantities.is: a domain or a half that makes it a function or one-to-one
quantities.pick: such as y = +√x from y² = x, or x ≥ 0 for x²

clean: the witness value is a small integer
graphs show the repeat clearly on grid points

line-conditions.name: A segment and a line built from it
line-conditions.summary: Pick two integer points first, then derive the gradient, the midpoint, a parallel or perpendicular line through a chosen point, its intercepts and its equation in every form, so any of them can be hidden.

quantities.name: A, B
quantities.is: two points, the ends of a segment
quantities.pick: integer coordinates with different x; the steps across and up give a gradient p/q with q at most 5

quantities.name: M
quantities.is: the midpoint of AB
quantities.pick: the average of the coordinates; both sums even so M has integer coordinates

quantities.name: m
quantities.is: the gradient of AB
quantities.pick: (y_B − y_A)/(x_B − x_A), never 0

quantities.name: n
quantities.is: the gradient of the new line
quantities.pick: m when parallel, −1/m when perpendicular

quantities.name: P
quantities.is: the point the new line passes through
quantities.pick: M (a perpendicular bisector), A, B, the origin, or another integer point

quantities.name: c
quantities.is: the y-intercept of the new line
quantities.pick: y_P − n·x_P

quantities.name: forms
quantities.is: y = nx + c, y − y_P = n(x − x_P), and ax + by + d = 0 with integers and a > 0
quantities.pick: scale y = nx + c by the denominator of n

quantities.name: intercepts
quantities.pick: both non-zero when the line is built from them

quantities.name: follow-on point
quantities.is: a point on the new line with one coordinate hidden
quantities.pick: integer x; y found by substituting, or the reverse

quantities.name: area
quantities.is: the triangle the new line makes with the axes

modes: two points (default): the line through A and B
point and gradient: P and n are given directly
parallel or perpendicular: n comes from a given line, written as y = mx + c or ax + by + d = 0
intercepts: the line through (p, 0) and (0, q)
parameter: one line contains k, found from a parallel or perpendicular condition
clean: integer points; gradients with denominator at most 5
the given gradient is non-zero, so the perpendicular gradient exists
when ax + by + d = 0 is asked, a, b, d are integers with no common factor and a > 0
on a graph, A, B and the intercepts sit on grid points

line-crossing.name: Two lines and where they meet
line-crossing.summary: Pick the meeting point first, then two lines through it with different gradients, so the solution is clean; a parallel mode gives equal gradients and no meeting point.

quantities.name: (X, Y)
quantities.is: the meeting point
quantities.pick: small integers, picked first

quantities.name: m₁, m₂
quantities.is: the two gradients
quantities.pick: different small integers or halves; equal in the parallel and same-line modes

quantities.name: lines
quantities.is: the two equations
quantities.pick: y = mx + c, or ax + by = k with integer coefficients, both through (X, Y)

quantities.name: parameter
quantities.is: an unknown constant in one line
quantities.pick: found from the meeting point, or the value that makes the lines parallel

quantities.name: third line
quantities.is: a line through the meeting point
quantities.pick: with a given gradient or through a second given point

modes: one point (default)
parallel: same gradient, different intercepts, so no meeting point
same line: one equation is a multiple of the other, so every point is shared
clean: Paper 1: integer meeting point
Paper 2: a decimal meeting point found with the GDC, to 3 s.f.

line-model.name: A straight-line model in context
line-model.summary: A fixed amount plus a steady rate: a taxi fare, a phone plan, a tank filling or draining, a spring stretching. Pick the rate and the start value, then derive the data, the table and the predictions.

quantities.name: context
quantities.is: what is modelled
quantities.pick: cost = fixed charge + rate × distance; volume = start ± rate × time; length = natural length + rate × mass

quantities.name: m
quantities.is: the rate: the amount per unit of input, with units
quantities.pick: one or two decimal places

quantities.name: c
quantities.is: the start or fixed amount: the output when the input is 0
quantities.pick: a friendly number

quantities.name: domain
quantities.is: the inputs the model makes sense for
quantities.pick: input ≥ 0, and up to where a tank is empty or full

quantities.name: data points
quantities.is: two (input, output) pairs from the context
quantities.pick: at friendly inputs, so the rate is clean

quantities.name: table
quantities.is: outputs at equally spaced inputs
quantities.pick: constant differences show the line

quantities.name: second model
quantities.is: a rival plan to compare with
quantities.pick: a different rate and fixed charge, with the plans equal at an integer input

clean: money to 2 d.p.
the comparison point is an integer input
one prediction lies outside the domain on purpose

transform-chain.name: A base graph and a chain of moves
transform-chain.summary: Pick a base function f and up to three moves in order, then derive g, the image of every key point and asymptote, and the new domain and range, so f, g, the moves or a point can be hidden.

quantities.name: f
quantities.is: the base function
quantities.pick: x², x³, √x, 1/x, eˣ, ln x or log₂ x, sin x, or a graph through labelled grid points

quantities.name: moves
quantities.is: the transformations
quantities.pick: up to three of: vertical stretch factor a, horizontal stretch factor 1/b, reflection in the x-axis (a < 0) or the y-axis (b < 0), translation by the vector (c, d)

quantities.name: order
quantities.is: the order the moves are applied in
quantities.pick: stated whenever it changes the result; Paper 1 uses at most two moves

quantities.name: g
quantities.is: the transformed function
quantities.pick: g(x) = a·f(b(x − c)) + d when the stretches and reflections come first and the translation last; other orders are built one step at a time

quantities.name: key points
quantities.is: labelled points on f: intercepts, a vertex, a turning point, an endpoint
quantities.pick: grid points

quantities.name: image points
quantities.is: where each key point goes
quantities.pick: (x, y) ↦ (x/b + c, a·y + d), chosen so every image is a grid point

quantities.name: asymptotes
quantities.is: the asymptotes of f and where they move
quantities.pick: x = p ↦ x = p/b + c; y = q ↦ y = a·q + d

quantities.name: domain and range of g
quantities.is: the moved domain and range
quantities.pick: the domain moves with the horizontal changes, the range with the vertical ones

quantities.name: disguise
quantities.is: g written so the moves are hidden
quantities.pick: expanded (x² − 6x + 4 = (x − 3)² − 5); a log law (log₂(8x) = log₂ x + 3); a factor inside the bracket (f(2x − 6) = f(2(x − 3)))

modes: forward (default): f and the moves given, g asked
describe: f and g given, the moves asked
undo: g and the moves given, f asked
point: a point and the moves given, its image or the point it came from asked
clean: stretch factors ±2, ±3 or ±1/2
translation components small integers
every image point and asymptote on the grid

fn-pre-expand.name: Brackets to expand
fn-pre-expand.summary: Small integer coefficients in one or two brackets, sometimes with a factor in front and a constant after.

quantities.name: brackets
quantities.is: the product to expand
quantities.pick: k(x + r)(x + s) + d, or k(x + r)² + d, with small integers

quantities.name: expanded
quantities.is: the result kx² + …
quantities.pick: computed from the brackets

clean: coefficients between −9 and 9
answers have at most three terms

fn-pre-factorise.name: An expression with known factors
fn-pre-factorise.summary: Pick the factors first, then expand, so the answer is known.

quantities.name: factors
quantities.is: the brackets
quantities.pick: common factor kx; (x − r)(x − s); (mx + r)(x + s); (px − q)(px + q)

quantities.name: expression
quantities.is: the expanded form shown
quantities.pick: computed from the factors

clean: r and s between −9 and 9
leading coefficient at most 6

fn-pre-surds.name: Surds built from a square factor
fn-pre-surds.summary: Pick a and a square-free b, then show √(a²b) or sums of such surds.

quantities.name: a, b
quantities.is: the simplest form a√b
quantities.pick: a from 2 to 6, b square-free from 2, 3, 5, 6, 7

quantities.name: shown
quantities.is: the surd or expression given
quantities.pick: √(a²b), sums, products, or (m ± √(a²b))/n with n dividing m and a

clean: every answer simplifies to integers and one surd

fn-pre-linear-inequalities.name: A linear inequality with a known boundary
fn-pre-linear-inequalities.summary: Pick the boundary and direction, then build ax + b compared with c.

quantities.name: boundary
quantities.is: where the inequality switches
quantities.pick: an integer or a simple fraction

quantities.name: sign of a
quantities.is: whether dividing reverses the sign
quantities.pick: negative in about half the items

quantities.name: form
quantities.is: one-sided or two-sided
quantities.pick: ax + b < c, or c₁ < ax + b ≤ c₂

clean: integer boundaries on Paper 1 style items

fn-pre-percent-multiplier.name: An amount changed by a percentage
fn-pre-percent-multiplier.summary: Pick an original amount and whole-number percentages, then compute the new amount, so any of them can be asked.

quantities.name: original
quantities.is: the amount before the change
quantities.pick: a round number such as 80, 250 or 1200

quantities.name: r
quantities.is: the percentage change
quantities.pick: a whole number from 1 to 40, up or down

quantities.name: multiplier
quantities.is: 1 + r/100 for an increase, 1 − r/100 for a decrease
quantities.pick: such as 1.05 for +5% and 0.85 for −15%

quantities.name: new amount
quantities.is: original × multiplier
quantities.pick: computed

quantities.name: repeats
quantities.is: the same or different changes one after another
quantities.pick: the multipliers multiply

clean: new amounts are whole numbers or have 2 decimal places
reverse questions give a whole-number original

fn-pre-graph-reading.name: A graph, a table and some decimals
fn-pre-graph-reading.summary: A graph on a grid with a chosen scale, a short table of points, and decimals to round, all picked so the right answer is known.

quantities.name: scale
quantities.is: what one grid square is worth on each axis
quantities.pick: 1, 2, 5, 0.1, 0.2 or 0.5 per square, often different on the two axes

quantities.name: points
quantities.is: marked or tabulated points
quantities.pick: on grid lines or halfway between them

quantities.name: decimals
quantities.is: numbers to round
quantities.pick: GDC-style values such as 2.0449, 0.004567, 1.4972, 13.96, with a digit that rounds up or a zero that must be kept

clean: each rounding item has exactly one right answer
read values sit on a grid line or exactly halfway

fn-pre-rearrange.name: A formula with a known rearrangement
fn-pre-rearrange.summary: Pick the formula and the new subject, so the rearranged form is known in advance.

quantities.name: formula
quantities.is: the formula given
quantities.pick: linear y = mx + c; a square or root such as y = x² + 9 or y = √(x + 4); a fraction such as y = 3/(x − 2); the subject twice, such as y = (2x + 1)/(x − 3)

quantities.name: subject
quantities.is: the letter to make the subject
quantities.pick: one that appears once, or twice

quantities.name: rearranged
quantities.is: the formula with the new subject
quantities.pick: computed from the formula

clean: small integer constants
at most one ± or one fraction in the answer

fn-pre-algebraic-fractions.name: Fractions with x in them
fn-pre-algebraic-fractions.summary: Pick the answer and the excluded values first, then build the fraction or equation from them.

quantities.name: fraction
quantities.is: the expression or equation shown
quantities.pick: a quotient with a factor to cancel, a sum of two fractions, or a + k/(x − h) = c

quantities.name: excluded values
quantities.is: the x that make a denominator zero
quantities.pick: small integers

quantities.name: answer
quantities.is: the simplified fraction or the solution
quantities.pick: computed from the build, checked by substituting a number

clean: coefficients between −9 and 9
solutions are integers and never an excluded value unless the item is about rejecting it

fn-pre-substitute.name: An expression and a value to put in
fn-pre-substitute.summary: Pick an expression with a power, a negative coefficient or a fraction, and an input that tests it.

quantities.name: expression
quantities.is: the expression to evaluate
quantities.pick: such as 3 − 2x, 2x², −x² + 4x, (x + 1)/(x − 1), x³ − 5

quantities.name: input
quantities.is: the value to substitute
quantities.pick: a negative integer, a simple fraction such as 1/2, or 0

quantities.name: value
quantities.is: the result
quantities.pick: computed with brackets round the input

clean: inputs from −5 to 5 or a simple fraction
results are integers or simple fractions

fn-pre-linear-equations.name: A linear equation with a known solution
fn-pre-linear-equations.summary: Pick the solution first, then build the equation around it.

quantities.name: solution
quantities.is: the value of x
quantities.pick: an integer, or a simple fraction in harder items

quantities.name: shape
quantities.is: how the equation looks
quantities.pick: ax + b = c; ax + b = cx + d; p(x + q) = r(x + s); x/p + x/q = r; a line ax + by = k to rearrange for y

clean: coefficients between −9 and 9
fractions have denominators 2 to 6

fn-pre-simultaneous.name: Two equations with a known solution
fn-pre-simultaneous.summary: Pick (x, y) first, then two equations through it.

quantities.name: solution
quantities.is: the pair (x, y)
quantities.pick: small integers

quantities.name: equations
quantities.is: the two equations shown
quantities.pick: one coefficient already matching; one equation to scale; both to scale; or a word problem (two kinds of ticket)

quantities.name: special case
quantities.is: no solution or infinitely many
quantities.pick: the second equation a multiple of the first on the left only, or on both sides

clean: coefficients between −9 and 9
one scaling by 2 or 3 is enough in most items

fn-link-transformations.name: One translation and stretch in several settings
fn-link-transformations.summary: Pick a vector (a, b) and a stretch factor first, then apply them to a parent graph, a data set, a normal curve, an area and an antiderivative, so the same move shows up in each.

quantities.name: vector
quantities.is: the translation (a, b): a across, b up
quantities.pick: small integers, a ≠ 0 or b ≠ 0

quantities.name: stretch
quantities.is: a factor m applied to outputs (or to data values)

quantities.name: parent
quantities.is: the graph that is moved
quantities.pick: x², 1/x, eˣ, sin x or x³

quantities.name: moved feature
quantities.is: where the key feature lands
quantities.pick: vertex, asymptotes, a maximum point, or the asymptote y = 0 moved to y = b

quantities.name: antiderivatives
quantities.is: F(x) + C₁ and F(x) + C₂ for one f(x)
quantities.pick: integer C values, so the gap C₂ − C₁ is the vertical move

quantities.name: data set
quantities.is: five to eight values with their mean, median, standard deviation and IQR
quantities.pick: integer mean; then every value + k, or × m then + k

quantities.name: normal curve
quantities.is: X ~ N(μ, σ²) and its standardised form Z = (X − μ)/σ
quantities.pick: integer μ and σ; bounds that give z to 2 d.p.

quantities.name: area
quantities.is: ∫ from p to q of f(x) dx, and the same area after a move
quantities.pick: a rational value such as ∫₀² x³ dx = 4

clean: every moved point has integer or simple-π coordinates
summary statistics change by whole numbers
areas are exact

fn-link-vectors.name: One displacement in several settings
fn-link-vectors.summary: Pick a vector first and use it as a graph translation, the vertex of a parabola, the shift of a sine wave, the direction of a line, or the step between two points.

quantities.name: vector
quantities.is: (a, b) in 2D, or (Δx, Δy, Δz) in 3D
quantities.pick: small integers; 3D steps with even parts and a whole-number length, e.g. (2, 4, 4) of length 6

quantities.name: graph
quantities.is: y = f(x) and its image y = f(x − a) + b
quantities.pick: parent x², 1/x, eˣ or a line

quantities.name: point and image
quantities.is: a point P on the graph and P + (a, b)
quantities.pick: integer coordinates

quantities.name: vertex form
quantities.is: y = k(x − h)² + c as y = kx² moved by (h, c)

quantities.name: wave
quantities.is: y = A sin(Bx + E) + D, which is y = A sin(Bx) moved by (−E/B, D)
quantities.pick: E/B a simple multiple of π

quantities.name: line
quantities.is: gradient p/q and direction vector (q, p)
quantities.pick: small integers, p/q in lowest terms

quantities.name: 3D points
quantities.is: A, B and the midpoint M
quantities.pick: M = A + half the step, B = M + half the step

quantities.name: delay
quantities.is: a displacement graph moved by (d, 0)
quantities.pick: d a whole number of seconds

clean: all points on grid points
phase shifts are multiples of π/6 or π/4
3D lengths are whole numbers

fn-link-rate-of-change.name: A rate of change in four forms
fn-link-rate-of-change.summary: Pick a rate m and a start value first, then show them as an arithmetic sequence, a line, a fitted regression line and a derivative; a curve with a tangent gives the instant version.

quantities.name: rate
quantities.is: m, the change in output per 1 step of input
quantities.pick: a small integer or a decimal with units in context

quantities.name: sequence
quantities.is: u_n = u₁ + (n − 1)d with d = m
quantities.pick: integer u₁; the points (n, u_n) lie on y = mx + (u₁ − m)

quantities.name: line
quantities.is: y = mx + c
quantities.pick: c = u₁ − m when it is linked to the sequence

quantities.name: regression line
quantities.is: y = ax + b fitted to data, in context
quantities.pick: a with units, e.g. litres per km

quantities.name: curve
quantities.is: y = kx² and a point x = a
quantities.pick: k = 1, 2 or 3, small integer a

quantities.name: chord
quantities.is: gradient from x = a to x = a + h
quantities.pick: for y = kx², k(2a + h)

quantities.name: tangent gradient
quantities.is: the limit of the chord gradient, f′(a)
quantities.pick: 2ka

clean: integer rates and starts
chord gradients for h = 0.1 and 0.01 are short decimals

fn-link-multiplicative-growth.name: One factor, applied again and again
fn-link-multiplicative-growth.summary: Pick a start value and a factor per period first, then write the value after n periods as a sequence term, a function value, a compound-interest formula and a graph.

quantities.name: start
quantities.is: P₀, the value at t = 0
quantities.pick: a round number: 400, 1000, 2000

quantities.name: factor
quantities.is: r = 1 ± p/100 per period
quantities.pick: p a whole percentage; growth (r > 1) or decay (0 < r < 1)

quantities.name: sequence
quantities.is: u_n = P₀ r^(n − 1) with u₁ = P₀
quantities.pick: so u_n is the value after n − 1 periods

quantities.name: function
quantities.is: A(t) = P₀ r^t
quantities.pick: A(n − 1) = u_n

quantities.name: compounding
quantities.is: k periods a year at an annual rate p%
quantities.pick: k = 1, 4 or 12; factor 1 + p/(100k) per period

quantities.name: continuous form
quantities.is: P₀e^(kt)
quantities.pick: e^k is the factor per unit of time

quantities.name: threshold
quantities.is: a target T
quantities.pick: chosen so the first whole period past it is clear, e.g. 400 × 0.8ⁿ < 100 first at n = 7

quantities.name: series
quantities.is: the sum of the terms
quantities.pick: converges only when |r| < 1

clean: factors are exact decimals
thresholds are not crossed exactly at a whole period
money to 2 d.p.

fn-link-inverses.name: A process and the process that undoes it
fn-link-inverses.summary: Pick a process and an input first, then follow the output back through the undo, noting when the undo needs a restricted domain or loses information.

quantities.name: process
quantities.is: what is done
quantities.pick: eˣ, 2ˣ, x² (x ≥ 0), cos x, d/dx, a normal probability P(X < x)

quantities.name: undo
quantities.is: the inverse process
quantities.pick: ln x, log₂ x, √x, arccos x, integration, inverse normal

quantities.name: point pair
quantities.is: (a, b) on the process and (b, a) on the undo
quantities.pick: e.g. (2, e²) on y = eˣ and (e², 2) on y = ln x

quantities.name: restriction
quantities.is: the domain that makes the process one-to-one
quantities.pick: x ≥ h for a parabola with vertex at x = h; [0, π] for cos

quantities.name: lost information
quantities.is: what the undo cannot recover
quantities.pick: the second angle, the negative root, or the + C

quantities.name: normal
quantities.is: X ~ N(μ, σ²) and a probability p
quantities.pick: integer μ and σ; p to 2 d.p.

clean: exact values on Paper 1 style items (ln, π/3 multiples)
inverse normal answers to 3 s.f.

fn-link-symmetry.name: A mirror and a pair of matching points
fn-link-symmetry.summary: Pick a mirror value m and a distance d first; the matching pair m − d and m + d then appears as two points on a parabola, two tails of a normal curve, two angles or two values of r.

quantities.name: mirror
quantities.is: the line or value everything is reflected in
quantities.pick: axis x = h; the mean μ; x = π/2 for sine; r = n/2 for nCr

quantities.name: pair
quantities.is: m − d and m + d
quantities.pick: integer d, or a multiple of π/6

quantities.name: parabola
quantities.is: axis x = h and a point (h − d, y)
quantities.pick: small integers

quantities.name: normal
quantities.is: X ~ N(μ, σ²) and P(X > μ + a) = p
quantities.pick: p a two-place decimal below 0.5

quantities.name: angles
quantities.is: θ and π − θ (same sine), θ and 2π − θ (same cosine)
quantities.pick: multiples of π/6, π/4, π/3

quantities.name: nCr
quantities.is: nCr = nC(n − r)
quantities.pick: n up to 12

clean: exact probabilities from symmetry, no GDC
exact trig values

fn-link-equivalent-forms.name: One object written several ways
fn-link-equivalent-forms.summary: Pick the object first (a quadratic, a log value, cos 2x, a power of x) and write it in every useful form, so a question can show one form and ask for another or ask which form helps.

quantities.name: quadratic
quantities.is: general, factorised and vertex forms of one parabola

quantities.name: identity
quantities.is: x² + bx + c ≡ (x + p)² + q
quantities.pick: even b so p is an integer

quantities.name: log value
quantities.is: one number as several log expressions
quantities.pick: e.g. ln 12 − ln 3 = ln 4 = 2 ln 2

quantities.name: cos 2x
quantities.is: 1 − 2sin²x, 2cos²x − 1, cos²x − sin²x
quantities.pick: the equation also has sin x or cos x, so one form gives a quadratic

quantities.name: power form
quantities.is: a/xⁿ written as ax⁻ⁿ
quantities.pick: n = 1, 2 or 3; fractions such as 1/(4x³) = (1/4)x⁻³

quantities.name: fake form
quantities.is: a near-miss that is not equivalent
quantities.pick: log(a + b) as log a + log b; ln 12/ln 3 as ln 4

clean: integer roots and vertex for the quadratic
trig equations with exact solutions in [0, 2π]

fn-link-extremes.name: An extreme value found several ways
fn-link-extremes.summary: Pick the extreme first (a vertex, a wave's peak, a cubic's turning point, an endpoint, or the point where a line touches) and build the function around it.

quantities.name: quadratic model
quantities.is: h(t) = at² + bt + c with its vertex
quantities.pick: e.g. −5t² + 30t + 8: peak 53 at t = 3, surd roots

quantities.name: wave
quantities.is: y = A sin(Bx) + D
quantities.pick: max D + |A|, min D − |A|; first max at Bx = π/2

quantities.name: cubic
quantities.is: f with f′ a factorisable quadratic
quantities.pick: e.g. x³ − 3x² − 9x + 2: max 7 at x = −1, min −25 at x = 3

quantities.name: closed interval
quantities.is: [p, q] containing a turning point
quantities.pick: one endpoint higher than the turning value

quantities.name: tangent line
quantities.is: y = mx + n touching y = x² + r
quantities.pick: n − r = −s², so m = ±2s, e.g. y = mx − 1 and y = x² + 3 give m = ±4

clean: integer extreme values
tangent contact points on grid points

fn-link-graph-vs-algebra.name: An equation as two graphs that meet
fn-link-graph-vs-algebra.summary: Pick two functions f and g first; their meeting points are the solutions of f(x) = g(x), which may or may not be reachable by algebra.

quantities.name: pair
quantities.is: f and g
quantities.pick: solvable by algebra (eˣ = 20, x² = 2x + 3), or not (eˣ = 4 − x)

quantities.name: meeting points
quantities.is: the solutions
quantities.pick: exact when algebra works; to 3 s.f. otherwise, e.g. eˣ = 4 − x at x ≈ 1.07

quantities.name: count
quantities.is: how many meeting points in a domain

quantities.name: rejected root
quantities.is: an algebraic root that is not a meeting point
quantities.pick: from a log equation: ln x + ln(x + 3) = ln 10 gives 2 and −5

quantities.name: region
quantities.is: the area between f and g
quantities.pick: needs the meeting points as limits, e.g. x² and 2x + 3 meet at −1 and 3, area 32/3

quantities.name: turning values
quantities.is: the heights where y = k changes the count
quantities.pick: e.g. x³ − 3x has turning values 2 and −2

clean: exact answers where algebra works
GDC answers to 3 s.f.
every solution inside the interval visible in a standard window

triangle.name: One triangle with its sides, angles and area
triangle.summary: Pick clean givens for the view (two sides and the angle between them, three sides, two angles and a side, two sides and a non-included angle, or an area with two of the rest), then solve the whole triangle from them, so every side, every angle and the area are known and any of them can be asked.

quantities.name: A, B, C
quantities.is: the angles at the vertices, in degrees
quantities.pick: whole numbers of degrees when given; every angle of the triangle from 20° to 140°, and A + B + C = 180°

quantities.name: a, b, c
quantities.is: the sides, with side a opposite angle A, b opposite B and c opposite C
quantities.pick: whole numbers from 3 to 20 when given; the rest solved from the givens

quantities.name: area
quantities.is: ½ab sin C = ½bc sin A = ½ca sin B
quantities.pick: a whole number when it is given (the backwards questions)

quantities.name: labels
quantities.is: which vertex plays which part
quantities.pick: the roles are dealt to A, B and C at random, so the asked side or angle can be any of the three

quantities.name: acute or obtuse
quantities.is: said in the question when an angle is found from an area
quantities.pick: from the angle; it is at least 10° away from 90°

clean: every angle of the triangle from 20° to 140°, so no triangle is a sliver
given sides are whole numbers from 3 to 20, and given angles whole numbers of degrees
the sine rule for an angle only when the side opposite the given angle is the longer of the two given sides, so exactly one triangle fits
an angle found from an area is at least 10° from 90°, so acute or obtuse is a real choice
the answer is worked out from the givens as shown, and is at least 0.02 of a unit in its third significant figure away from a rounding edge, so its 3 s.f. value is not in doubt
every wrong option differs from the answer to 3 s.f.

types.name: Straight line from conditions, then use it
types.summary: Build a line from two points, a point and a gradient, a parallel or perpendicular condition, or its two intercepts; then use the line to find an unknown coordinate or an area.

representations.how: a line as y = mx + c or ax + by + d = 0
coordinates and conditions stated in words: "through (1, 4), perpendicular to AB"
the points or the line drawn on a grid
points on the line listed as a table of x and y

unknowns.asked: the gradient
the gradient
the gradient

given: one coordinate of a second point
unknowns.asked: the other coordinate
the gradient of a line perpendicular to it
the equation in the stated form
the equation of the line through them
the midpoint, then the line through it and another point (often the origin)
the equation of the line
the parallel line through the point
the perpendicular line through the point
the perpendicular bisector of the segment
unknowns.note: the exam splits it into midpoint, gradient and line

given: a point on it with one coordinate unknown
unknowns.asked: the unknown coordinate

given: y = mx + c with a fractional m, or a point and gradient
unknowns.asked: ax + by + d = 0 with integer coefficients
the x- and y-intercepts
the area of the triangle it makes with the axes
whether they are parallel, perpendicular or neither, with a reason

given: two lines, one with a constant k
unknowns.asked: k so that they are perpendicular (or parallel)

angles.name: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)
angles.about: Subtract the coordinates in the same order and divide the change in y by the change in x.

angles.name: Rearrange to y = mx + c and read off m
angles.about: Make y the subject; the coefficient of x is the gradient.

angles.name: Use m = −a/b for ax + by + d = 0
angles.about: For a line in general form the gradient is −a/b, so no rearranging is needed.

weak.why: two points must be worked out from the equation before there is anything to count

angles.name: Count rise over run on the graph
angles.about: Pick two grid points on the line, count the vertical and horizontal steps between them and divide, taking the sign from the direction of the line.

angles.name: Point-gradient form y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)
angles.about: Substitute the gradient and the known point into y − y₁ = m(x − x₁), then rearrange to the form the question asks for.

angles.name: Substitute the point into y = mx + c to find c
angles.about: Put the known gradient into y = mx + c, substitute the point's coordinates and solve for c.

angles.name: Translate y = mx by the vector (x₁, y₁)
angles.about: The line of gradient m through the origin, moved by the vector (x₁, y₁), is y − y₁ = m(x − x₁): replace x with x − x₁ and add y₁.

weak.why: it needs two points; the perpendicular line is known only by one point and a gradient

angles.name: Linear regression through the two points
angles.about: Enter the two points as data and run linear regression; with exactly two points the GDC returns the exact line, which checks the algebra.

angles.name: Set x = 0 for the y-intercept, y = 0 for the x-intercept
angles.about: Each intercept lies on an axis, so substitute 0 for the other coordinate and solve.

weak.why: only quick when the line is already y = mx + c; from ax + by + d = 0 it needs rearranging first

angles.name: Read c from y = mx + c
angles.about: In y = mx + c the y-intercept is (0, c) at sight and the x-intercept is (−c/m, 0).

angles.name: Cover-up method for ax + by = k
angles.about: Hide the y-term to get x = k/a and hide the x-term to get y = k/b.

weak.why: a fractional intercept such as 7/3 cannot be read exactly from a sketch

angles.name: Read the crossing points from the graph
angles.about: Locate where the line crosses each axis on a sketch or GDC graph; the GDC zero function gives the x-intercept.

angles.name: Use m₁ × m₂ = −1
angles.about: Multiply the gradients: perpendicular lines give −1, so an unknown gradient or parameter k comes from solving m₁m₂ = −1.

angles.name: Flip and change the sign
angles.about: The perpendicular gradient to m is −1/m; a parallel line keeps m; then use a point to finish the equation.

angles.name: Rotate the direction vector by 90°
angles.about: A line with direction (1, m) turned a quarter-turn has direction (−m, 1), so its gradient is −1/m.

weak.why: the segment is given by two points, not as ax + by + d = 0, so there are no coefficients to keep or swap until the line is written

angles.name: Keep a and b for parallel, swap them for perpendicular
angles.about: A line parallel to ax + by + d = 0 is ax + by + e = 0 and a perpendicular one is bx − ay + e = 0; substitute the point to find e.

angles.name: Average each coordinate

concepts.prompt: The lines 2x + 3y = 6 and 3x − 2y = 1 are perpendicular.
concepts.answer: True. The gradients are −2/3 and 3/2, and (−2/3) × (3/2) = −1.

concepts.prompt: A straight line meets both axes.
concepts.answer: Sometimes. A horizontal line such as y = 3 never meets the x-axis, and a vertical line such as x = 2 never meets the y-axis. Every other line meets both (at the same point if it passes through the origin).

concepts.prompt: In ax + by + d = 0, d changes while a and b stay the same. What happens to the line?
concepts.answer: It slides without turning: the gradient −a/b does not change, so the new line is parallel to the old one. The intercepts −d/a and −d/b grow or shrink in step with d.

concepts.prompt: If f(2) = 5 and f has an inverse, then f⁻¹(5) = 2.
concepts.answer: True. The point (2, 5) is on f, so (5, 2) is on f⁻¹: the inverse sends each output back to the input that made it.

concepts.prompt: A table shows f(1) = 4, f(4) = 2 and f(2) = 7. Predict whether (f∘f)(1) equals f(1) × f(1). Then work it out.
concepts.answer: No. (f∘f)(1) = f(f(1)) = f(4) = 2, while f(1) × f(1) = 16. Composing feeds one output in as the next input; it does not multiply.

concepts.prompt: The graph of f rises steadily from (−2, 1) to (4, 7). State the domain and range of f⁻¹ and say why.
concepts.answer: Domain 1 ≤ x ≤ 7 and range −2 ≤ y ≤ 4. Every point (p, q) on f becomes (q, p) on f⁻¹, so the x-values and y-values swap roles.
